notes.M1: Two broken-line examples show centre/lane boundaries; crossing is not a safety guarantee.
notes.M2: Short dashes at outer edge identify edge line, distinct from middle guidance dashes.
notes.M3: Long strokes/short gaps warn crossing unsuitable and possibly continuous line ahead.
notes.M4: Short central dashes guide complex junction path; not an exclusive cycle-lane boundary.
notes.M5: Dense tiny strokes mark cycle-lane boundary.
notes.M6: Thicker broken strokes mark public-transport lane boundary; actual permitted users must be checked.
notes.M7: Paired broken rows delimit a reversible lane controlled for current direction.
notes.M8: One continuous line in exact artwork matches neutral description and legal crossing restrictions. Shared variant falsely describes both single and double examples: DEF-10E-002.
notes.M9: Hatched diverging area normally excludes vehicles subject only to specified legal exceptions.
notes.M10: Solid line below broken examples restricts drivers on solid-line side.
notes.M11: Solid plus long warning dashes retains distinct restriction versus unsuitability.
notes.M12: Long warning dashes below shorter centre dashes preserve side-dependent warning.
notes.M13: Thick transverse bar states where a required stop occurs, not independent universal stop duty.
notes.M14: Four downward triangles identify yielding line; not a forced stop.
notes.M15: Parallel crossing stripes are pedestrian marking; signal control still matters.
notes.M16: Two rows of square blocks alone do not distinguish cycle passage/crossing; B8/M14 establish crossing.
notes.M17: Checkerboard bands cover hump/dip or similar obstacle, not raised hump only.
notes.M17a: Bicycle and advanced area identify positioning for cycles/class-II mopeds without granting priority.
notes.M18: Outlined inverted triangle gives advance stop/give-way information, unlike filled M14 triangles.
notes.M19: Four lane-arrow examples guide next junction; continuous-line duty and reserved-lane exception preserved.
notes.M20: Bent white arrow requires prompt safe lane change.
notes.M21: Continuous yellow edge means no stopping/parking.
notes.M22: Broken yellow edge means no parking and may show bus-stop extent.
notes.M23: Yellow zigzag reinforces M21/M22; exact applicable prohibition must be identified.
notes.M24: Three-sided white boundary outlines parking space; broken form is also legally possible.
